text:
tina_finance: FYI Aurora Metrics sent final pricing for our telemetry/embedding pilot. A few billing flags — can ops/ML/procurement sanity-check before I escalate?

marco_procure: Share the highlights.

tina_finance: Key bits from the quote: monthly commit 800 vGPU-hrs @ $4.75/hr; burst charges at 1.8x; embeddings billed as $0.0007 per vector-hour or $0.00003 per vector-request (mode selected per workload); onboarding $12k refundable only if commit met within 60 days; invoices in EUR to EU bank.

evan_ml: The dual embedding mode again  need definition of "vector-hour" vs "vector-request". For our heavy-batch reranker, per-request is better; but if their vector-hour counts cached in-memory vectors, cost might be massive.

grace_ops: Also want to know whether KV/cache hits are excluded. If every served vector counts even when read from cache, that doubles/triples our bill.

ted_legal: From contract side: reject non-reciprocal price-change clauses, require price-lock for first 12 months, add SLA credit & rollback language. Also insist invoices be in USD or have fixed FX protection for 12 months.

vendor_rep: Quick clarifications: (1) vector-hour = unique vector instances held or computed per hour; cache hits not billed if served from customer-managed KV, (2) burst threshold at 130% commit then 1.8x, (3) onboarding refundable only if commit reached. Happy to provide sample invoice.

evan_ml: Please provide the exact algorithm for computing "unique vector instances" (hashing rules, tolerance for near-duplicates). Also provide sample billing lines for a batched 10k-request job.

marco_procure: Procurement asks: (A) convert onboarding fee to usage credit prorated over 90 days if commit hit, (B) cap burst overage exposure during pilot to $20k, (C) Net-30 payment and invoice in USD to our US entity.

tina_finance: Add: require monthly CSV export that maps telemetry IDs to billed units and an API endpoint for raw usage data. Also quarterly audit right with adjustment clause if discrepancy >1.5%.

grace_ops: Ops ask: console toggle to disable overages beyond PO cap and programmatic webhook when burst > 100% of commit so we can auto-fallback.

ted_legal: I'll draft redline language for price-lock, FX, and SLA credits. Vendor rep, please confirm you can accept audit right and API access for enterprise customers.

vendor_rep: We can provide usage API and sample invoices. Audit rights OK within standard privacy bounds; will confirm acceptable SLA credit mechanics.

procurement_bot: Tagging vendor-contract & vendor-eval. Reminder: attach quote, sample invoice, and usage API spec. Decision milestone 2024-09-01.

marco_procure: I'll consolidate asks and send to vendor by EOD. If they won't accept pilot caps, we propose a capped pilot PO for $25k with explicit overage opt-out.

tina_finance: Thanks all  please keep the replies short; procurement wants bullet points for the vendor email.

evan_ml: Draft snippet for technical ask I can send:

"Please provide: 1) formal definition of 'unique vector instance' including hashing and dedup rules, 2) sample invoice mapping for a 10k-batch rerank job showing both modes, 3) usage API schema (proto/json), and 4) confirmation that cache/KV reads are excluded from billed units."

marco_procure: Copying that into the vendor email. Will ping when sent. :thumbsup:
